prompt: Our security audit flagged the CI deploy role as far too broad, and I agree. Please tighten its policy in infra/iam/ci-deploy-policy.json down to what this deploy tooling really does, for both staging and production, without breaking any deploy or rollback. Stage settings are in config/staging.json and config/production.json; the deploy is scripts/deploy.js and the rollback is scripts/rollback.js. Every cloud call goes through scripts/lib/cloud-client.js, and createFakeClient(calls) there records each call as { action, resource, params }, which may help you see what is used. Keep the deploy({ stage, client, releaseId }) and rollback({ stage, client, version }) interfaces as they are. Change only the policy: not the scripts, config, workflow, packages or the public site. Keep the file valid IAM policy JSON.

rubric.criterion: The permission entries are organized so a reviewer can tell which deploy operation each resource grant supports (code cannot check this because the evaluator checks decisions, not the policy's explanatory structure).

verdicts.note: The prompt describes what to deliver (a tightened IAM policy) without prescribing a named method, checklist, or process for how to work.

All hidden tests derive from the prompt's explicit requirements: stage resources from config files, actions from deploy.js and rollback.js, production-only CDN refresh, Lambda-only role passing. The staging distribution denial test correctly follows from 'Production refreshes its CDN but staging does not'.

No fixture comments, docs, or tests reveal the solution. The fixture has intentionally broad permissions; the answer requires reading deploy.js and rollback.js to identify specific actions and resources.

Reviewer passed it, but the draft prompt gave away the traps (production-only CDN refresh, rollback alias updates, PassRole limited to Lambda). The lead rewrote the prompt, and split the one all-calls test into deploy and rollback tests so a policy that drops the rollback path loses a test of its own (3 of 17 pass on the fixture).

All requirements are stated in the prompt: read config files and scripts, allow needed actions on specific resources, deny everything else, restrict role passing to Lambda service with a condition. No hidden knowledge required.
